discovery: Discovery of geometric and topological phases in quantum mechanics (the Aharonov-Bohm effect and the Berry phase)

nominees.name: Yakir Aharonov
nominees.affiliation: Tel Aviv University and Chapman University

motivation: Aharonov (with the late David Bohm) showed in 1959 that electromagnetic potentials, not only fields, have direct physical consequences: charged particles acquire a measurable phase when encircling a flux they never touch. Berry showed in 1984 that any quantum system transported slowly around a closed loop in parameter space acquires a geometric phase fixed by the loop's geometry alone. Both began as questions many considered meaningless and both have been confirmed precisely, including Tonomura's electron-holography tests. Together they established that quantum mechanics is inherently geometric and topological. That idea now underlies the theory of the quantum Hall effect, topological insulators and Chern numbers, polarization in solids, anyonic statistics, and geometric quantum gates. Few theoretical insights have changed so completely how physicists think about the quantum state or opened so many experimental fields.
